title: inline-attn-orchestrator: in-place rotary fusion + KV-hinting for continuous-batcher
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: multiple production workloads show a tail of small-sequence requests that trigger a suboptimal code path: separate rotary application and KV cache maintenance cause additional memory copies and synchronization between the continuous-batcher and the attention microkernel. This PR introduces an inline "attn-orchestrator" that performs in-place rotary/rope application fused with the attention kernel entry points and emits lightweight KV-maintenance hints for the continuous-batcher. Goals: 1) eliminate an allocation+memcpy for rotary application on the common fp16 path; 2) let the batcher preemptively place/reuse KV storage slots via hints instead of reactive eviction; 3) provide a safe quantized fallback path for int8/4 FlashAttention variants when the fused path is not supported on a device.

What changed (high level): implemented an in-place rotary applier that integrates directly into the FlashAttention entry sequence, added a small ABI for KV-hint emission (kv_hint_t) used by the continuous-batcher, extended the kernel-selection logic to prefer the fused path for sequences <= 512 and batch sizes >= 4, and added an int8-compatible kernel shim that delegates to quantized flash when AVX/SM-specific intrinsics are present. Also updated tests, bench harness, and runtime metrics to capture hint utilization and fused-path hit-rate.
commits: a1e5b2c: introduce attn_orchestrator ABI and kv_hint_t structure
b4f7d9e: implement inplace_rotary_applier and integrate into flash_entry_fp16
c3d2f11: add quantized shim and selection heuristics (w/ unit tests)
e5f6a7c: bench: microbench continuous-batcher with real workload traces
f1b2c3d: docs and release notes; change log
diff_snippets: runtime/attn/flash_entry_fp16.cc: replaced rotary_apply(buffer) call with rotate_inplace(buffer, seq_len) to avoid extra buffer allocation
scheduler/continuous_batcher/kv_hints.h: added kv_hint_t {slot_id, expected_size, lifecycle_hint} and API emit_kv_hint(request_id, kv_hint_t)
runtime/attn/quant_shim_int8.cc: thin wrapper to call quantized_flash::run when fused path not supported
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Overall this looks promising. Can you justify the heuristics for seq_len <= 512? Bench numbers would be helpful across 128/256/512/1024 to ensure no regressions.

Asha Menon: Added bench results in bench/micro/attn_fused_bench.py and included a table in docs/perf/fused-attn-orchestrator.md showing 15-28% p99 latency reduction and ~12% token cost improvement in the 128-512 range. For 1024 there is a small regression on some card types due to register pressure; we fall back to standard flash in that case.
Priya Shah: The kv_hint ABI seems lightweight, but I'm concerned about thread-safety when the batcher reuses slots. Can we document lock ordering and provide an assert in debug builds?

Asha Menon: Added assert and a brief doc section. The hint is advisory — batcher validates slot ownership with an epoch check before reuse. Documented in scheduler/continuous_batcher/kv_hints.h comments.
Liam O'Connor: Are there memory-safety implications for in-place rotary on pinned buffers used by async GPU copies?
Asha Menon: We added a pinned-buffer guard: if buffer->is_pinned() we fall back to the copy-path. This is guarded in orchestrator.cpp and tested in tests/attn/test_inplace_rotary.py.
Diego Alvarez: CI flake on windows build; looks like a path issue in quant_shim - reran and passed.
CI Bot: All checks passed on rerun.
release_notes: Performance: Introduce inline-attn-orchestrator that fuses in-place rotary application with the attention kernel and provides KV hints to the continuous-batcher. Typical improvements: 12% token-cost reduction and 15-28% p99 latency reductions for 128-512 sequence workloads in fp16 on supported hardware. Fallbacks ensure correctness for larger sequences and pinned buffers.
notes_for_ops: Operators: To enable fused path on Dedicated clusters, ensure runtime flag --enable-inline-attn is set (off by default until v1.18 rollout). Quantized shim requires the quantized runtime package (quant-runtime) to be present on nodes. Telemetry emits attn.fused_path_hit_rate and attn.kv_hint_utilization; recommend adding alarms for fused_path_hit_rate drop > 30% during rollout.
changelog_entry: Perf: fused rotary+attn kernel and KV-hint integration; improved continuous-batcher reuse behavior
testing_summary: Unit tests added for inplace_rotary edge cases (pinned buffer fallback, seq boundary). Microbench harness run against production traces; integration tests exercised quantized fallback on an Ampere A10 and an older T4 (validated no correctness regression).
